data.body:
Merged into dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 and closed as a duplicate. Nothing from this epic was dropped.

dabb survived as canonical because it carries the architecture this one did not specify: a registry of category-tagged check objects, crash isolation so one check raising cannot abort the run, per-check timeouts on anything touching network/auth, chezmoi-style severity tiers, an explicit exit contract (gate on the fatal tier only; warnings never fail), and a prior-art survey with a ranked list of gotchas to design against.

What THIS epic contributed, now absorbed verbatim into dabb:
- The framing: several independent diagnostic surfaces (validate, fsck, bridge-fsck, the local-dev-env manual checks) with no single entry point, so a user has to already know which tool to reach for.
- The concrete check inventory for configuration (unknown config keys, conflicting gate settings), environment (stale global rebar shadowing the repo venv, unwired pre-commit hook, missing commit-msg hook in a fresh worktree, missing [agents] extra, missing API tokens), and ticket data (orphans, cycles, unknown event types from a newer store, stale reducer caches, malformed attestations).
- A FIFTH category dabb did not have: sync artifacts — bridge-fsck bindings, PUSH_PENDING, bridge probe failures.
- The auto-repair boundary: unambiguous and reversible only; never silently rewrite ticket events, resolve bridge duplicates, or change rebar.toml without confirmation.
- The AC that existing surfaces keep working standalone and doctor COMPOSES them rather than replacing them.

Work on `rebar doctor` should now happen on dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6.
